ic_name: SD Memory Card (SD Simplified Physical Layer Specification)

fields.spec_version: SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 (April 10, 2017)

spec_lineage_sd.summary: Initial Simplified release; basic SD Memory Card, classic SDSC ≤ 2 GB; Default Speed (25 MHz).
Added High Capacity Memory Card (SDHC, > 2 GB up to 32 GB), Speed Class 2/4/6, CMD8 SEND_IF_COND voltage handshake, High Speed mode 50 MHz.
Added Extended Capacity Memory Card (SDXC, > 32 GB up to 2 TB), Ultra High Speed I (UHS-I) with 1.8 V signaling and SDR12/25/50/104 + DDR50 modes, Speed Class 10, UHS Speed Grade 1, Current Limit.
Added UHS-II Interface (differential lanes on a separate pin row), UHS Speed Grade 3, Power Limit, Function Extension Specification.

Added Discard and FULE to Erase, Card Ownership Protection (COP) for Card Lock/Unlock, Application Performance Class A1/A2, Cache, Self-Maintenance, Command Queueing, Simplified Mechanical Drawings, Simplified Bus Timings.

spec_lineage_mmc_emmc_sibling.summary: Original MultiMediaCard; 3.3 V; up to 20 MHz; CMD1 init handshake (no ACMD41).
Embedded MMC; 3.3 V / 1.8 V; 4-bit or 8-bit DAT; high speed 52 MHz.
Added HS200 (200 MHz single-data-rate) + boot partition + RPMB.
Added Command Queueing (CQ) and Secure Removal.

key_changes.summary: SDHC / block addressing — argument to CMD17/CMD24/CMD25 is in 512-byte blocks for SDHC/SDXC, not in bytes.
UHS-I — adds 1.8 V signaling, SDR12/25/50/104 + DDR50, mandatory CMD19 tuning for SDR104, CMD11 voltage switch.
UHS-II — differential lanes on the back side of the card; out of the 9-pin standard pad assignment.
Adds CQ (Command Queueing), Cache, Self-Maintenance, A1/A2 Application Performance Class, COP (Card Ownership Protection).

backward_compat_traps.rule: Argument to CMD17/CMD24/CMD25 is BYTE address for SDSC and BLOCK address (512 B units) for SDHC/SDXC.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Drivers written for SDSC that forget to check OCR.CCS will silently misaddress SDHC/SDXC cards (offset off by a factor of 512).

backward_compat_traps.rule: CMD8 is only valid on v2.0+ cards; v1.x cards return no response and host shall not retry indefinitely.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Host that fails to handle CMD8 no-response will hang on v1.x cards.

backward_compat_traps.rule: CMD16 (SET_BLOCKLEN) sets block length for read on SDSC; on SDHC/SDXC the read block length is fixed at 512 B and CMD16 is silently accepted but ignored.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Drivers attempting 1024 B or 2048 B blocks on SDHC will get 512 B blocks back without error.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Card shall complete init within 1 second; host shall loop ACMD41 until OCR.BUSY=1 or 1-second timeout.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Hosts with no timeout will hang on a defective card.

backward_compat_traps.rule: MMC uses CMD1 SEND_OP_COND directly; SD uses CMD55 + ACMD41. CMD1 to an SD card returns illegal command.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Auto-probing hosts must distinguish SD (ACMD41) from MMC (CMD1) by first issuing CMD8 (v2.0 SD) or by trying ACMD41 first and falling back to CMD1 only on illegal-command response.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Holding CS LOW during CMD0 transitions the card permanently into SPI mode.
backward_compat_traps.trap: An SD-mode host that accidentally drives CS LOW at power-up will lose access to SD-mode commands until card is re-powered.

backward_compat_traps.rule: After CMD11 voltage switch, there is no way back to 3.3 V signaling without a full power cycle.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Voltage-switch failure recovery requires VDD power-cycle, not software reset.

fields.version_naming_history_note: The SD Memory Card is managed by the SD Card Association (SDA) and its IP holder consortium SD-3C, LLC (a 3-way joint venture of Panasonic, SanDisk, and Toshiba). 'Simplified' specs are public subsets of the full normative SDA spec released for industry adoption. eMMC is the sibling embedded MMC family managed by JEDEC; the SD and eMMC command-line protocols share the same 48-bit CMD frame structure and similar register set, but differ in initialization (ACMD41 vs CMD1), pin assignment (eMMC adds DAT4..DAT7 and RST_n; no card-detect), and high-speed modes (UHS-I vs HS200/HS400).
